I am 66 years old and have farmed these fields for 35 years. My father taught me, and now my wife and I manage our 4.1 mu plot together. We have always done wheat-maize rotation here in Quzhou — it is what the land and climate allow. I did not go far in school, but I know my soil and my crops.

For wheat, I will plant my usual improved variety in early October after rotary tillage. I buy my wheat seed from the village supply shop — it is not the old traditional seed, but a reliable improved kind that gives steady yields. I will put down compound fertilizer as a base before sowing, and then top-dress with urea in the spring when the wheat greens up. With my well, I can irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. That is enough — electricity for pumping is not cheap, and at my age I cannot manage endless trips to the fields. I will spray herbicide once and maybe one more spray for aphids or rust if I see trouble. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed directly after the wheat harvest in early June — no-tillage, using the machine service that comes through the village. Everyone here uses hybrid maize now; the yield is much better than the old types. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing, and if the rains are poor I will irrigate twice — at sowing and at the big trumpet stage. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide at sowing and one insecticide spray later when the borers come. I expect around 550 kg per mu. My wife and I are only two people now, so we keep things simple and stick to what has worked for decades.
